title: KCET 2015 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q:
The unit cell with crystallographic dimensions, a $
eq$ b $
eq$ c, $\alpha$ = $\gamma$ = 90$^\circ$ and $ eta 
eq$ 90$^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: A unit cell with all edges unequal and two angles 90 deg while the third is not 90 deg is the monoclinic system.

questions.q: While charging the lead storage battery, ________.
options: PbSO$_4$ on anode is reduced to Pb
PbSO$_4$ on cathode is reduced to Pb
PbSO$_4$ on cathode is oxidized to Pb
PbSO$_4$ on anode is oxidized to PbO$_2$
questions.explanation: The Pb plate is conventionally called the anode and the PbO$_2$ plate the cathode; on recharging (electrolysis) the reactions reverse, so PbSO$_4$ on the anode (Pb plate) is reduced back to Pb.

questions.q: Adenosine is an example of
questions.explanation: Adenosine is adenine (a purine base) linked to ribose sugar without a phosphate group, which makes it a nucleoside (a nucleotide would additionally have a phosphate group).

questions.q: Orlon has monomeric unit
questions.explanation: Orlon (polyacrylonitrile) is the addition polymer of vinyl cyanide (acrylonitrile), CH$_2$=CH-CN.

questions.q: The two electrons have the following set of quantum numbers : P = 3, 2, -2, +$\dfrac{1}{2}$ ; Q = 3, 0, 0, +$\dfrac{1}{2}$. Which of the following statement is true?
options: P and Q have same energy
P has greater energy than Q
P has lesser energy than Q
P and Q represent same electron
questions.explanation: P (n=3, l=2) is a 3d electron and Q (n=3, l=0) is a 3s electron; using the (n+l) rule, 3d (n+l=5) has higher energy than 3s (n+l=3), so P has greater energy than Q.

questions.q: H$_2$O$_2$ cannot oxidise
questions.explanation: Ozone (O$_3$) is a stronger oxidising agent than H$_2$O$_2$, so H$_2$O$_2$ cannot oxidise O$_3$; instead O$_3$ oxidises H$_2$O$_2$ to O$_2$ and H$_2$O.

questions.q: In the given set of reactions, 2-Bromopropane $\xrightarrow[\text{alc./heat}]{\text{AgCN}}$ X $\xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4}$ Y, the IUPAC name of product 'Y' is
questions.explanation: AgCN (covalent) reacts with alkyl halides through nitrogen to give an isocyanide (isopropyl isocyanide, X); LiAlH$_4$ reduces the isocyanide to a secondary amine (CH$_3$)$_2$CH-NH-CH$_3$, whose IUPAC name using the longer propane chain as parent is N-methylpropan-2-amine.

questions.q: On heating with concentrated NaOH solution in an inert atmosphere of CO$_2$, white phosphorous gives a gas. Which of the following statement is incorrect about the gas?
options: It is less basic than NH$_3$.
It is more basic than NH$_3$.
It is highly poisonous and has smell like rotten fish.
It's solution in water decomposes in the presence of light.
questions.explanation: The gas evolved is phosphine (PH$_3$), which is a much weaker base than NH$_3$ (lone pair in a larger, more s-character orbital); so the statement that it is 'more basic than NH$_3$' is incorrect.

questions.q: Sodium metal crystallizes in B.C.C. lattice with edge length of 4.29 Å. The radius of sodium atom is
questions.explanation: For a BCC lattice, r = ($\sqrt{3}$/4)a = 0.433 $\times$ 4.29 Å $\approx$ 1.857 Å.

questions.q: 0.06% (w/v) aqueous solution of urea is isotonic with
questions.explanation: 0.06 g urea (M=60) per 100 mL = 0.6 g/L / 60 g mol$^{-1}$ = 0.01 M; isotonic solutions have equal molar concentration, so the matching glucose solution is 0.01 M.

questions.q: In a first order reaction, the concentration of the reactant is reduced to 12.5% in one hour. When was it half completed?
questions.explanation: 12.5% remaining = 1/8 = (1/2)$^3$, i.e. 3 half-lives occur in 60 minutes, so one half-life = 20 minutes.

questions.q: The electrolyte having maximum flocculation value for AgI/Ag$^+$ sol. is
questions.explanation: AgI/Ag$^+$ sol is positively charged, so the coagulating anion of lowest charge is least effective and needs the highest concentration (highest flocculation value); among Cl$^-$, S$^{2-}$, SO$_4^{2-}$ and PO$_4^{3-}$, the monovalent Cl$^-$ (NaCl) has the maximum flocculation value.

questions.q: Copper is extracted from Copper pyrites by heating in a Bessemer converter. The method is based on the principle that
options: Copper has more affinity for oxygen than Sulphur at high temperature.
Iron has less affinity for oxygen than Sulphur at high temperature.
Copper has less affinity for oxygen than Sulphur at high temperature.
Sulphur has less affinity for oxygen at high temperature.
questions.note: The standard textbook answer is 'Copper has less affinity for oxygen than sulphur' (option 3): this is why, after FeS is slagged off, the self-reduction step 2Cu$_2$O + Cu$_2$S \rightarrow 6Cu + SO$_2$ proceeds — oxygen preferentially combines with sulphur, not copper. The KEA key marks the opposite statement (option 1) as correct.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Bessemerization of copper matte relies on the differing affinities for oxygen: KEA's key credits 'copper has more affinity for oxygen than sulphur' as the operating principle.

questions.q: Which of the following will be able to show geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: Tetrahedral complexes are too symmetric to show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism, and MA$_3$B square planar has only one possible arrangement; a square planar MABCD complex with four different ligands can have distinct cis/trans arrangements and shows geometrical isomerism.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of Gd$^{2+}$ is (at. no. of Gd is 64)
questions.explanation: Neutral Gd is [Xe]4f$^7$5d$^1$6s$^2$; removing 2 electrons for Gd$^{2+}$ removes the two 6s electrons first, giving [Xe]4f$^7$5d$^1$.

questions.q: MSO$_4$ $\xrightarrow{\text{NH}_4\text{OH}}$ $\downarrow$X (white) $\xrightarrow[\text{excess}]{\text{NH}_4\text{OH}}$ Y $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{S}}$ $\downarrow$Z. Here M and Z are
questions.explanation: ZnSO$_4$ with NH$_4$OH gives a white precipitate of Zn(OH)$_2$ (X); excess NH$_4$OH dissolves it to the soluble complex [Zn(NH$_3$)$_4$]$^{2+}$ (Y); passing H$_2$S then precipitates white ZnS (Z), so M = Zn and Z = ZnS.

questions.q: The hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane with aqueous NaOH result in the formation of
questions.explanation: A secondary halide like 2-bromobutane reacts by a mixture of SN1 and SN2 pathways, so the chiral centre is partially inverted and partially retained, giving a racemic mixture, ($\pm$) butan-2-ol.

questions.q: The distinguishing test between methanoic acid and ethanoic acid is
questions.explanation: Methanoic (formic) acid has an aldehydic -CHO group and gives a positive Tollens' silver-mirror test, while ethanoic (acetic) acid does not, so Tollens' test distinguishes them.

questions.q: In H$_2$ – O$_2$ fuel cell the reaction occurring at cathode is
questions.explanation: In an alkaline H$_2$-O$_2$ fuel cell, reduction of oxygen occurs at the cathode: O$_2$ + 2H$_2$O + 4e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ 4OH$^-$.

questions.q: Which of the following curve is in accordance with Freundlich adsorption isotherm? [Graphs: (1) x/m vs p rising then flattening to a plateau; (2) x/m vs p rising slowly then curving up steeply; (3) log(x/m) vs log p as a straight line with a gentle slope and a clear positive y-intercept; (4) log(x/m) vs log p as a straight line with a steep slope passing almost through the origin]
options: x/m vs p, steeply rising curve
log(x/m) vs log p, straight line with gentle slope and positive intercept
log(x/m) vs log p, straight line with steep slope through the origin
questions.explanation: The Freundlich isotherm x/m = kp$^{1/n}$ gives, on taking log, log(x/m) = log k + (1/n)log p, a straight line on a log(x/m) vs log p plot with slope 1/n (<1) and a positive y-intercept log k, matching curve (3).

questions.q: How many ions per molecule are produced in the solution when Mohr salt is dissolved in excess of water?
questions.explanation: Mohr's salt, FeSO$_4$.(NH$_4$)$_2$SO$_4$.6H$_2$O, is a double salt that dissociates completely into Fe$^{2+}$ (1) + 2NH$_4^+$ (2) + 2SO$_4^{2-}$ (2) = 5 ions.

questions.q: Glycogen is
options: structurally very much similar to amylopectin
structurally similar to amylopectin but extensively branched
questions.explanation: Glycogen, the storage polysaccharide in animals, has a structure like amylopectin (branched chains of $\alpha$-D-glucose) but is far more extensively branched.

questions.q: Number of possible alkynes with formula C$_5$H$_8$ is
questions.explanation: The three possible alkynes of formula C$_5$H$_8$ are pent-1-yne, pent-2-yne and 3-methylbut-1-yne.

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solution has the highest freezing point?
questions.explanation: Freezing point depression depends on effective particle concentration (i $\times$ C); 0.01 M NaCl gives the lowest effective concentration (0.02) among the options, so it has the smallest depression and hence the highest freezing point.

questions.q: Half life period of a first order reaction is 10 min. Starting with initial concentration 12 M, the rate after 20 min is
questions.explanation: k = 0.693/10 = 0.0693 min$^{-1}$; after 20 min (2 half-lives) concentration falls from 12 M to 3 M, so rate = k[A] = 0.0693 $\times$ 3 M min$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The salt which responds to dilute and concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ is
questions.explanation: Ba(NO$_3$)$_2$ reacts with both dilute and concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ to give a white precipitate of highly insoluble BaSO$_4$, the reaction being driven to completion by the very low solubility of BaSO$_4$ regardless of acid strength/concentration.

questions.q: On heating potassium permanganate, one of the following compound is not obtained:
questions.explanation: On heating, 2KMnO$_4$ decomposes to K$_2$MnO$_4$ + MnO$_2$ + O$_2$; MnO is not formed in this decomposition.

questions.q: $\bigcirc$-Br + Mg $\xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}}$ A $\xrightarrow[\text{H}^+]{\text{H}_2\text{O}}$ B. (cyclohexyl bromide reacting with Mg then aqueous acid) The product 'B' is
questions.explanation: Cyclohexyl bromide with Mg in dry ether forms the Grignard reagent A (cyclohexylmagnesium bromide); simple aqueous acid workup (protonolysis, not addition to a carbonyl) converts the highly basic C-Mg bond directly into a C-H bond, giving cyclohexane (B).

questions.q: The formation of cyanohydrin from a ketone is an example of
questions.explanation: The cyanide ion (a nucleophile) adds across the polar C=O bond of the ketone to give a cyanohydrin, which is a nucleophilic addition reaction.

questions.q: One of the following is an essential amino acid.
questions.explanation: Isoleucine cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained from the diet, making it an essential amino acid, unlike tyrosine, cysteine and serine which are non-essential.

questions.q: The aqueous solution of following salt will have the lowest pH:
questions.explanation: HClO$_4$ is the strongest acid among HClO, HClO$_2$, HClO$_3$ and HClO$_4$, so its conjugate base ClO$_4^-$ hydrolyses the least; a NaClO$_4$ solution stays closest to neutral (lowest pH among these basic salt solutions).

questions.q: For one of the element various successive ionization enthalpies (in kJ mol$^{-1}$) are given below: I.E. 1st=577.5, 2nd=1810, 3rd=2750, 4th=11,580, 5th=14,820. The element is
questions.explanation: The very large jump between the 3rd and 4th ionization enthalpies shows only 3 valence electrons, and the magnitude of IE$_1$ (577.5 kJ/mol) matches aluminium.

questions.q: 0.30 g of an organic compound containing C, H and Oxygen on combustion yields 0.44 g CO$_2$ and 0.18 g H$_2$O. If one mol of compound weighs 60, then molecular formula of the compound is
questions.explanation: Mass of C = 0.44$\times$12/44 = 0.12 g, mass of H = 0.18$\times$2/18 = 0.02 g, mass of O = 0.30-0.12-0.02 = 0.16 g; mole ratio C:H:O = 0.01:0.02:0.01 = 1:2:1 gives empirical formula CH$_2$O (mass 30); since molar mass is 60, molecular formula is C$_2$H$_4$O$_2$.

questions.q: One of the following amide will not undergo Hoffmann bromamide reaction:
questions.explanation: The Hofmann bromamide degradation requires a primary amide (RCONH$_2$) with two N-H bonds; CH$_3$CONHCH$_3$ is an N-substituted (secondary) amide and cannot undergo this reaction.

questions.q: Cheilosis and digestive disorders are due to the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Deficiency of riboflavin (vitamin B$_2$) causes cheilosis (cracking at the corners of the mouth) along with digestive disorders.

questions.q: How many Coulombs of electricity are required for the oxidation of one mol of water to dioxygen?
questions.explanation: 2H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ O$_2$ + 4H$^+$ + 4e$^-$ transfers 4 mol electrons per 2 mol water, i.e. 2 mol electrons per mol water; charge = 2 $\times$ 96500 C = 1.93 $\times$ 10$^5$ C.

questions.q: 100 cm$^3$ of 1 M CH$_3$COOH was mixed with 100 cm$^3$ of 2 M CH$_3$OH to form an ester. The change in the initial rate if each solution is diluted with equal volume of water would be
questions.explanation: Esterification is second order overall, rate = k[acid][alcohol]; diluting both reactants to half their concentration reduces the rate to (1/2)$\times$(1/2) = 0.25 times the original.

questions.q: Which of the following colloids cannot be easily coagulated?
questions.explanation: Macromolecular (lyophilic) colloids are extensively solvated and need very large amounts of electrolyte to coagulate, so they cannot be easily coagulated.

questions.q: The complex ion having minimum magnitude of $\Delta_0$(CFSE) is
questions.explanation: In the spectrochemical series Cl$^-$ is a weaker-field ligand than H$_2$O, NH$_3$ and CN$^-$, so [Co(Cl)$_6$]$^{3-}$ causes the smallest crystal field splitting $\Delta_0$.

questions.q: The arrangement of following compounds: i. bromomethane ii. bromoform iii. chloromethane iv. dibromomethane, in the increasing order of their boiling point is
questions.explanation: Boiling point rises with molecular mass/number and size of halogen atoms: chloromethane (-24$^\circ$C) < bromomethane (3.6$^\circ$C) < dibromomethane (97$^\circ$C) < bromoform (149$^\circ$C), i.e. iii < i < iv < ii.

questions.q: Iodoform can be prepared from all, except
questions.explanation: The iodoform test needs a CH$_3$CO- group or a CH$_3$CH(OH)- group; propan-1-ol (a primary alcohol without this arrangement) does not give a positive iodoform test, unlike the other three compounds.

questions.q: Identify 'Q' in the following sequence of reactions: cyclohexyl methyl ketone (ring with -COCH$_3$) $\xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5}$ P $\xrightarrow[\text{excess}]{\text{NaNH}_2}$ Q [Options are ring substituted with: (1) -CH=CH$_2$ (vinyl), (2) =CH$_2$ (exocyclic alkene), (3) -C$\equiv$CH (ethynyl), (4) -COCH=O]
questions.explanation: PCl$_5$ converts the ketone C=O into a gem-dichloride (P); excess NaNH$_2$, a strong base, then causes double dehydrohalogenation to give a terminal alkyne, ring-C$\equiv$CH (Q).

questions.q: Cryolite is
options: Na$_3$AlF$_6$ and is used in the electrolysis of alumina for decreasing electrical conductivity.
Na$_3$AlF$_6$ and is used in the electrolysis of alumina for lowering the melting point of alumina only.
Na$_3$AlF$_6$ and is used in the electrolysis of alumina for lowering the melting point and increasing the conductivity of alumina.
Na$_3$AlF$_6$ and is used in the electrolytic refining of alumina.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Cryolite (Na$_3$AlF$_6$) is added in the Hall-Héroult process to lower the melting point of alumina and to increase the electrical conductivity of the melt.

questions.q: Which of the following compound of Xenon has pyramidal geometry?
questions.explanation: XeO$_3$ has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair on Xe (sp$^3$ hybridisation), giving it a trigonal pyramidal shape, unlike the linear XeF$_2$, square pyramidal XeOF$_4$ or square planar XeF$_4$.

questions.q: After adding non-volatile solute freezing point of water decreases to $-$0.186 $^\circ$C. Calculate $\Delta T_b$ if K$_f$ = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$ and K$_b$ = 0.521 K kg mol$^{-1}$
questions.explanation: $\Delta T_f$ = 0.186 K gives molality m = $\Delta T_f$/K$_f$ = 0.186/1.86 = 0.1; then $\Delta T_b$ = K$_b$ $\times$ m = 0.521 $\times$ 0.1 = 0.0521 K.

questions.q: Plot of Maxwell's distribution of velocities is given below: [Two curves of fraction of molecules vs molecular velocity; the T$_2$ curve is taller and narrower, peaking at a lower velocity V$_2$ with higher fraction f$_2$; the T$_1$ curve is shorter and broader, peaking at a higher velocity V$_1$ with lower fraction f$_1$.] Which of the following is correct about this plot?
questions.explanation: Raising the temperature broadens the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve, lowers its peak height and shifts the peak to a higher velocity; since the T$_1$ curve is broader/flatter with its peak at the higher velocity V$_1$, T$_1$ is the higher temperature, so T$_1$ > T$_2$.

questions.q: The pair of compound which cannot exist together in solution is
questions.explanation: NaHCO$_3$ and NaOH react together (NaHCO$_3$ + NaOH $\rightarrow$ Na$_2$CO$_3$ + H$_2$O), so they cannot coexist in solution.

questions.q: What amount of dioxygen (in gram) contains 1.8 $\times$ 10$^{22}$ molecules?
questions.explanation: Moles of O$_2$ = 1.8$\times$10$^{22}$/6.022$\times$10$^{23}$ $\approx$ 0.03 mol; mass = 0.03 $\times$ 32 g/mol $\approx$ 0.960 g.

questions.q: Using MOT, compare O$_2^+$ and O$_2^-$ species and choose the incorrect option.
options: O$_2^+$ have higher bond order than O$_2^-$.
O$_2^+$ is diamagnetic while O$_2^-$ is paramagnetic.
Both O$_2^+$ and O$_2^-$ are paramagnetic.
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory O$_2^+$ (bond order 2.5) has one unpaired electron in $\pi^*$ and O$_2^-$ (bond order 1.5) also has one unpaired electron, so both are paramagnetic; the statement that O$_2^+$ is diamagnetic is incorrect.

questions.q: Which of the following is not true?
options: Ampicillin is not a natural antibiotic.
Prontosil is not converted into sulphanilamide in the body.
Vancomycin is a broad spectrum antibiotic.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Prontosil is a prodrug that is in fact metabolised in the body to the active antibacterial agent sulphanilamide, so the statement that it is 'not converted' is false — making it the 'not true' statement.

questions.q: In the reaction S + $\dfrac{3}{2}$O$_2$ $\longrightarrow$ SO$_3$ + 2x kJ and SO$_2$ + $\dfrac{1}{2}$O$_2$ $\longrightarrow$ SO$_3$ + y kJ, heat of formation of SO$_2$ is
questions.explanation: By Hess's law, the direct path (S+O$_2$$\rightarrow$SO$_2$, releasing h) followed by (SO$_2$+½O$_2$$\rightarrow$SO$_3$, releasing y) must release the same total heat as the direct route S+3/2O$_2$$\rightarrow$SO$_3$ (releasing 2x); so h + y = 2x, giving the heat of formation of SO$_2$ as h = 2x − y. This question was awarded a grace mark by KEA.

questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their acidic strength: i. m-nitrophenol ii. m-cresol iii. phenol iv. m-chlorophenol
questions.explanation: The electron-donating methyl group of m-cresol reduces acidity below phenol; the electron-withdrawing inductive effect of Cl in m-chlorophenol raises acidity above phenol; the strong resonance and inductive electron-withdrawal of the nitro group makes m-nitrophenol the most acidic, giving ii < iii < iv < i.

questions.q: In the sequence of reactions: P $\xrightarrow[\text{(2) Sn/HCl}]{\text{(1) Br}_2}$ Q $\xrightarrow[\text{(2) H}_2\text{O/H}_3\text{PO}_2]{\text{(1) NaNO}_2\text{/HCl, 273-278 K}}$ R $\xrightarrow[\text{OH}^-]{\text{KMnO}_4}$ o-bromobenzoic acid (COOH and Br on adjacent ring carbons), the starting compound 'P' is
questions.explanation: Starting from p-nitrotoluene, both the -CH$_3$ (o,p-director) and -NO$_2$ (m-director) direct bromination to the position ortho to CH$_3$; Sn/HCl reduces -NO$_2$ to -NH$_3$, diazotisation (NaNO$_2$/HCl) followed by H$_3$PO$_2$ removes the -NH$_2$ (deamination) to give o-bromotoluene (R), whose methyl group is then oxidised by KMnO$_4$/OH$^-$ to give o-bromobenzoic acid.

questions.q: Acetic acid is treated with Ca(OH)$_2$ and the product so obtained is subjected to dry distillation. The final product is
questions.explanation: Acetic acid with Ca(OH)$_2$ forms calcium acetate, which on dry distillation undergoes ketonic decarboxylation to give propanone (acetone).

questions.q: The correct statement is
options: BF$_3$ is the strongest Lewis acid among the other boron halides.
BI$_3$ is the weakest Lewis acid among the boron halides.
There is maximum p$\pi$ – p$\pi$ back bonding in BF$_3$.
There is minimum p$\pi$ – p$\pi$ back bonding in BF$_3$.
questions.explanation: Fluorine's 2p orbital size matches boron's 2p orbital best, giving maximum p$\pi$-p$\pi$ back bonding in BF$_3$ (which is why BF$_3$ is actually the weakest and BI$_3$ the strongest Lewis acid among the boron trihalides).

questions.q: Which of the following compound possesses the "C – H" bond with the lowest bond dissociation energy?
questions.explanation: Homolysis of a benzylic C-H bond in toluene gives a resonance-stabilised benzyl radical, which lowers its bond dissociation energy below that of aromatic, primary or secondary C-H bonds in the other options.

questions.q: In presence of HCl, H$_2$S results the precipitation of Group-2 elements but not Gp-4 elements during qualitative analysis. It is due to
questions.explanation: HCl provides a common H$^+$ ion that suppresses the ionisation of the weak acid H$_2$S (common-ion effect), lowering the S$^{2-}$ concentration enough to exceed only the low K$_{sp}$ of Group-2 sulphides, not the more soluble Group-4 sulphides.

questions.q: One of the following conversion results in the change of hybridization and geometry:
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ is sp$^2$ hybridised and trigonal planar, while BF$_4^-$ is sp$^3$ hybridised and tetrahedral, so this conversion changes both the hybridisation and the geometry (unlike NH$_3$$\to$NH$_4^+$ or H$_2$O$\to$H$_3$O$^+$, which stay sp$^3$).

questions.q: Water softening by Clark's process uses
questions.explanation: Clark's process softens temporary hard water by adding a calculated amount of slaked lime, Ca(OH)$_2$, which converts soluble Ca(HCO$_3$)$_2$/Mg(HCO$_3$)$_2$ into insoluble carbonates.

questions.q: An alkali metal hydride (NaH) reacts with diborane in 'A' to give a tetrahedral compound 'B' which is extensively used as reducing agent in organic synthesis. The compounds 'A' and 'B' respectively are
questions.explanation: NaH reacts with B$_2$H$_6$ in diethyl ether (A) to give the tetrahedral reducing agent sodium borohydride, NaBH$_4$ (B).
